advances: A sufficient mixed-depth bound for prescribed homothetic fibers and a finite Jensen-affine approximation; arbitrary translation defects are outside the tolerance conclusion.

proof:
For $q_p>0$, membership of $a_p-b_p$ in $\gamma_J(a_p-b_p)J$ and convexity of $J$ give $a_p+q_pJ\subset b_p+r_pJ=K_p$. The cores are used only at sites of $E$. If $E$ is empty, any actual point gives the zero bound.

For $E\ne\varnothing$, let $G$ be the convex hull of $(p,a_p)$ for $p\in E$, and let $P_E=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(E)$. By completeness, $P_E$ is the full integer set of $\operatorname{conv}(E)$. Every representation of $j\in P_E$ by points of $E$ yields continuous coordinate $a_j$ by the Jensen property. Thus $G$ has exactly the singleton $(j,a_j)$ over each such site, and this point is feasible in the original convex set because every $(p,a_p)$ for $p\in E$ belongs to its core. Let $T$ be the set of these integer graph points. For each convex test in the graph ambient space, its trace on $T$ is identified by projection with the trace on $P_E$ of its intersection with $G$. Indeed the projected intersection is convex and every relevant graph fiber is a singleton. This gives $h(T)\le h(P_E)$. Also $h(P_E)\le h(P)$ since a family of convex tests on $P_E$ can be intersected with $\operatorname{conv}(E)$ and treated on $P$.

Assign weights $q_p^d$ to $(p,a_p)$ for $p\in E$ and zero to the other points of $T$. Apply 6d6fcf377e68c79c to the finite closed set $T$ and its finite Borel measure of positive total $\sum_{p\in E}q_p^d$. The selected point of $T$ has at least $\sum_{p\in E}q_p^d/h(P)$ weight in every closed halfspace containing it. At a counted site $p$ that halfspace either includes the entire core or restricts to a closed halfspace containing $a_p$. By homothety, its core volume is then at least $\beta q_p^d|K|_d$. Summing and dividing by the original mass $|K|_d\sum_p r_p^d$ proves the bound, even if the chosen graph site has zero core weight.

The uniform gauge bound gives $q_p\ge(1-\varepsilon)r_p$. The claimed tolerance follows by taking $d$th roots of $\beta(1-\varepsilon)^d\ge\Gamma_d$. The Jensen-affine assignments form a closed linear subspace in the finite product of the site coordinates, and the objective is continuous. Since $J$ contains a ball about zero and is contained in a bounded ball, its gauge is continuous and bounded below by a positive multiple of Euclidean norm. The objective is therefore coercive on the subspace, giving attainment. At a symmetry center the ordinary depth is $1/2$ by reflection and zero hyperplane volume. For $d\ge2$ the binomial expansion gives $(1+1/d)^d>2$, hence $\Gamma_d<1/2$. The ordinary attainment and rigidity theorem 03bc771bddd39a8a gives maximum strictly above $\Gamma_d$ exactly off the simplex class. Any maximizing point is interior since a supporting closed halfspace at a boundary point captures zero $d$-volume.

statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite. Suppose a compact convex set has actual integer fibers $K_p=c_p+r_pK$ with $r_p>0$ for $p\in P$, with no positive $d$-volume at other integer sites. Fix $t\in\operatorname{int}K$ and let $\beta$ be the normalized ordinary closed-halfspace depth of $t$ in the uniform body $K$. Put $J=K-t$ and $b_p=c_p+r_pt$. Let $a:P\to\mathbb R^d$ preserve every anchored convex representation of a site of $P$ by sites of $P$. With $\gamma_J$ the Minkowski gauge of $J$, put $q_p=(r_p-\gamma_J(a_p-b_p))_+$. Then some actual mixed point has normalized depth at least
$$
\frac{\beta}{h(P)}\frac{\sum_{p\in P}q_p^d}{\sum_{p\in P}r_p^d},
$$
where $h(P)$ is the relative Helly number. If $E=\{p:q_p>0\}$ is nonempty, the point can be taken on the graph of $a$ above $\operatorname{conv}(E)\cap P$.

In particular, if $\gamma_J(a_p-b_p)\le\varepsilon r_p$ for every $p$ and $0\le\varepsilon<1$, the depth is at least $\beta(1-\varepsilon)^d/h(P)$. With $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, this gives $\Gamma_d/h(P)$ when $\varepsilon\le1-(\Gamma_d/\beta)^{1/d}$. For fixed $t$ the infimum of $\max_p\gamma_J(a_p-b_p)/r_p$ over the Jensen-affine assignments $a$ is attained. If $K$ is centrally symmetric its center has $\beta=1/2$, yielding positive tolerance for $d\ge2$. More generally a nonsimplex $K$ admits an interior $t$ with $\beta>\Gamma_d$, while a simplex has maximum ordinary depth $\Gamma_d$.
title: Weighted depth transfer from Jensen-affine homothetic cores
